businessRules.rule: A staff record is created only when a candidate whose appointment letter has been accepted actually joins, or by migration at go-live. There is no route that types a person straight into employment, in the same way that a student record is created only by an approved admission.

The role, agreed salary and pay basis, start date, notice period and any probation carry across from the accepted letter rather than being typed again, since retyping is where a figure quietly changes between what was agreed and what is paid. Completing the record is not creating an employee — the creation was already authorised by the accepted letter.

Classification is the employment category the record carries — teaching or non-teaching, and permanent, contract, probation or part-time. It is not decoration: leave management reads it for leave entitlement and payroll reads it for how the employee is paid, so every value it can take has to be defined.
The monthly paid leave allowance is recorded on the record, and leave beyond it is unpaid. Both payroll and leave management work from this one figure.
An emergency phone number is required and is not the employee's own. A number that reaches only the person who has collapsed is not an emergency contact.

The documents the employee hands over on joining are recorded against the record — identity document, degrees, experience certificates and references. Each is recorded as received with the date and the name of the person who verified it. Recording receipt is what makes the joining checklist work.

A document is scanned where the school holds scans of that type, which is a decision taken per document type rather than a blanket rule. An identity document held as a scan carries the access restriction and retention rule that the security module governs.
The record is approved before it is saved to the staff roster. Who approves is a configuration; by default it is the Principal. A change made by the approving role itself needs no second approval.
Accounts read the record for payroll and cannot change it. The role that calculates pay must not be the role that sets what it is calculated from.

The record carries a state — active, on notice, or inactive. It is deactivated and never deleted, because payroll history, ledger entries and audit trails reference it. Payroll pays active records only, so a departed employee stops being paid on the leaving date set by the exit process.
A fixed-term contract carries an end date, and the record is flagged as that date approaches. A contract that lapsed unnoticed leaves somebody working without one.
The salary amount is not an ordinary field on this record. It is set separately and is visible only to the roles the visibility rule names.
The statutory identifiers are further fields on this same record, captured by the same people at the same time. They are not a separate feature.
The identity number and the email are unique across staff. Two records sharing either is the commonest way a duplicate is created.
An employee sees their own record and may request a correction to it, but cannot change it themselves.

transitions.condition: Completed on the joining date with every required field and document recorded.
Approved. The record joins the staff roster and payroll pays it (BR-8, BR-10).
Returned with a reason. The person is not on the roster.
A change is submitted for approval (BR-8).
The change is approved, or returned and the record stands as it was.
A resignation or termination is approved and the notice period runs.
The leaving date arrives. Payroll stops paying the record (BR-10).
The notice period is cancelled and the employee returns to normal status.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → HR → Staff → Complete a record from an accepted letter
basicFlow.userAction: Opens the record from the accepted appointment letter on the joining date, once the candidate has attended.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Carries the role, agreed salary and pay basis, start date, notice period and any probation across from the letter rather than requiring them to be typed again.

basicFlow.navigation: Complete staff record → Personal and contact detail
basicFlow.userAction: Completes the personal and contact detail — name, guardian name, photograph, gender, date of birth, identity number, contacts, emergency number, email, designation, working hours, joining date, contract end date where fixed-term, salary account and statutory identifiers.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the identity number and email are unique, and that the emergency number differs from the employee's own.

basicFlow.userAction: Sets the classification — teaching or non-teaching, and permanent, contract, probation or part-time.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires one of the defined values, since leave entitlement and pay both read it.

basicFlow.userAction: Records how many paid leaves the employee gets each month.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Stores the one figure both payroll and leave management will read.

basicFlow.navigation: Complete staff record → Record documents received
basicFlow.userAction: Records each document handed over — identity document, degrees, experience certificates and references — with the date and the person who verified it, and scans it where the school holds scans of that type.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires a verifier on every document, and applies the access restriction to an identity scan.

basicFlow.navigation: Complete staff record → Submit for approval
basicFlow.systemResponse: Routes it to whichever role the configuration names, the Principal by default.
Sets the record active and adds it to the staff roster, which attendance, leave and payroll then read.

basicFlow.navigation: HR → Staff record → Edit → Submit change for approval
basicFlow.userAction: Changes a detail as circumstances change, giving a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Routes the change through the same configured approval, keeping the previous value.

alternateFlows.condition: The record is being migrated at go-live
alternateFlows.behaviour: Existing staff are brought in by migration rather than from a letter, since no appointment letter exists for them (BR-1).

alternateFlows.condition: The approver does not accept the record
alternateFlows.navigation: Record approvals → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns with a reason and the person is not on the staff roster. Nothing reads an unapproved record (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The change is made by the approving role itself
alternateFlows.behaviour: It needs no second approval, since the person who would approve it has made it (BR-8).
An end date is required, and the record is flagged as that date approaches so a contract does not lapse unnoticed (BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: The school does not hold scans of that document type
alternateFlows.behaviour: The document is recorded as received and verified without a scan. Scanning is a decision per document type (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The employee spots an error in their own record
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → HR → My record → Request a correction
alternateFlows.behaviour: They raise a correction request. They cannot change the record themselves (BR-15).

alternateFlows.condition: The employee resigns or is terminated
alternateFlows.behaviour: The record moves to on notice and then to inactive on the leaving date, and payroll stops paying it (BR-10).

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
